correctness.rationale: Off-diagonal resolvent positivity reduces the complete entrywise sign question to one Fourier diagonal G_n(s). Strict decreasing in s gives a unique crossing; nonnegative/stochastic holds exactly through it. Periodized 2D heat kernels and strict Bessel-index monotonicity give G_n>G_(n+1), while the classical square-lattice Green integral yields the limiting elliptic formula. The geometric resolvent bound, a verified mean Laplacian eigenvalue 4, and derivative lower bound prove exponential size convergence. n=3 exact quadratic and test computations have been checked on package code; finite computations are explicitly not proof of all n. The claims exclude anisotropic, Dirichlet, and nonlinear extensions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a general sufficient CFL bound nor the 1D tridiagonal exact theorem dominates a sharp all-n two-dimensional periodic result; changing boundary and dimension changes the resolvent diagonal. An entirely general graph criterion for diagonal resolvents reduces the question but does not supply the explicit roots, ordering and exponential rate. Historical unpublished or inaccessible stronger coverage cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: The problem determines exactly when a standard two-dimensional periodic heat timestep preserves nonnegative data; this is a substantive physical/numerical property not guaranteed by A-stability. The theorem supplies sharp finite-grid thresholds, strict grid-size ordering, a nontrivial classical elliptic thermodynamic value, and a proved exponential convergence estimate. The limiting admissible physical step ~0.5882 exceeds the elementary nonnegative-stencil sufficient bound 0.5, and the finite thresholds exceed even this thermodynamic value. This is a natural invariant and network-size law rather than arbitrary tabulation.
